verdict.rationale: Anytype documents its own choices for where data lives: local-only on-device storage, Anytype's default backup infrastructure, or a self-hosted network (with a team-maintained docker image). Self-hosting gives users effective residency control. However, no region or residency picker is documented for Anytype's hosted backup nodes. Switching network mode also requires exporting channels and re-importing them into a new identity. missing for 10: region selection for Anytype-hosted storage, documented residency guarantees for the default infrastructure, seamless switching between storage modes, independent corroboration of self-hosted residency.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: To back up your channels and data to a self-hosted network, you need to have a network configuration.
If you prefer to fully keep your data on your device without any server to sync between your desktop and mobile, you can enable local-only mode.
You can work completely offline, sync across your own devices, or self-host your data.
export all your channels, and import them into a new identity after switching the network mode
